answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a costly, verifiable stake: before an agent earns reputation, it must lock a deposit that is slashed if peers detect duplicate behavior. Think of a jetty where every boat pays a mooring fee before docking - cheap for one real vessel, ruinous for a thousand fake ones. A lotus grows one stem per root; likewise, one stake should support one identity, and a vine of attestations from independent, staked peers should be required before new agents can transact. Copying identities then costs more than it can earn.
